sections.normalized_html: The length of a cross-country skiing course is [MATH: 12] kilometers. How long is the course in meters?

sections.normalized_html:
We need to convert [MATH: 12] kilometers into meters.

We start with the unit conversion between kilometers and meters:

[MATH: 1\, \textrm{kilometer} = 1,000 \, \textrm{meters}]

The left-hand side reads [MATH: 1] kilometer, and we want to determine how many meters there are in [MATH: {\color{blue}{12}}] kilometers. So, we multiply both sides of the above equation by [MATH: {\color{blue}{12}}.]

[MATH: 12 × 1kilometers|= 12 × 1, 000meters; 12kilometers|= 12, 000meters]

Therefore, [MATH: 12] kilometers equals [MATH: 12,000] meters.

sections.normalized_html:
We need to convert [MATH: 78] centimeters into millimeters.

We start with the unit conversion between centimeters and millimeters:

[MATH: 1 \,\textrm{cm} = 10 \,\textrm{mm}]

The left-hand side reads [MATH: 1] centimeter, and we want to determine how many millimeters there are in [MATH: 78] centimeters. So, we multiply both sides of the above equation by [MATH: 78.]

[MATH: 78 × 1cm|= 78 × 10mm; 78cm|= 780mm]

Therefore, [MATH: 78\,\textrm{cm}] equals [MATH: 780\,\textrm{mm}.]
